newsitem.title: USA: Cargill to close physical cocoa trading in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Cargill to close physical cocoa trading in U.S.

text.p: Cargill Inc, one of the largest commodity trading firms in the world, is getting out of the physical cocoa trading business in the United States, a company spokesman confirmed on Wednesday.
"Physical cocoa trading in the West has not been able to produce a return on investment which is desireable," the spokesman said. "It does not seem that it will change."
The privately-held, Minneapolis-based Cargill anticipates it will take about one year to unwind the company's positions in the U.S.
The spokesman added, however, that all of Cargill's other cocoa operations will continue, and that Cargill's commitment to cocoa remains "firm."
Cargill's physical cocoa trading based in the Netherlands, and its processing operations in the U.S., Netherlands and Brazil will all continue, he said.
